gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-nobile: Heavy, rounded strokes in Plakkaat curl their terminals nearly back to the stem, while Nobile stays open and tight to its caps. Closed against open is the whole story.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic gives the page a modern, clean footing, with a gap in the c and capitals barely above lowercase. Noto Kufi Arabic is the quiet partner here, while Plakkaat's uniform, heavy line does the shouting.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans: Noto Sans fills most of each letter's height with lowercase body and keeps its c wide open. Noto Sans keeps a long page moving smoothly under Plakkaat's heavy, closed-in lettering, which looks drawn with a single pen tip.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Chunky and curled, then wide open. Plakkaat's terminals loop back toward the stem, and Noto Sans Adlam lets its curve endings stay well apart, so a long passage feels easy and unhurried with tall, full c, s and z.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-adlam-u: Wire-cut heft up top, open curves below. Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined leaves generous space between curve ends and stems, and that gap against Plakkaat's nearly closed terminals is the pair's real hook.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-anatoli: Modern, with a lot of weight. Plakkaat is built to hit hard with closed, heavy shapes, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs does its best work in outward-pointing terminals and an x-height rising near cap height.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic reads clean and modern, with wide openings on small letters and a pronounced x-height. Noto Sans Arabic carries a long page easily beneath Plakkaat's closed, heavy letters, which are drawn with one constant line width.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-armenia: Noto Sans Armenian reads approachable and professional, with tall, full c, s and z and a wide, inviting opening on its round letters. Plakkaat's closed, rolling-ball-pen heaviness sits above it, so a long page feels welcoming.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Modern and clean, with a push-pull. Plakkaat's heavy terminals nearly close on the stem, while Noto Sans Avestan keeps its curve tips apart under a pronounced x-height, and that closed-versus-open tension is what makes the pair.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-balines: Pipe-like strokes, thick and rounded, with plenty of presence. Noto Sans Balinese opens a breathing space inside every curve and keeps its ascenders short, which makes the pairing's contrast of closed against open its strongest card.
